about: Everything the Linkling service stores, and for how long (ADR-0004, ADR-0011, ADR-0012). tests/privacy-manifest.test.ts fails unless the fields below are exactly the database's columns; linkling-web's privacy page carries every what, kept, counted and logged text below word for word, and its checks/privacy-matches-service.sh fails when it does not.

stored.what: The address the link sends people to
The maker's name, as they gave it (often their computer login name)
When the link stops working, if its maker gave it an end
An internal number for the link
stored.kept: Until the link is deleted; its daily counts keep the number after that

stored.what: For each link and each calendar day (in UTC, the same clock for everyone), how many times the link was followed that day
stored.kept: Forever, even after the link is deleted. A deleted link's counts stay under its internal number, tied to no name, and are shown nowhere

stored.what: The highest internal link number handed out so far, so that no number is used twice

counted: A link's count for the day goes up by one each time someone opening it is sent on to its target. Opening a link that does not exist or has expired adds nothing, and neither does a tool that only checks whether a link works without opening it. Chat apps and other programs often open a pasted link by themselves, to show a preview or to check that it is safe, and those count too: telling them apart from people would mean reading something about each visitor, which Linkling does not do.
logged: The service writes no access log, and handling a request writes nothing about it to any log.
